title: Tucatinib + capecitabine + trastuzumab

agents.name: Tucatinib
agents.explanation: Tucatinib reduces signalling from the internal part of HER2. It works alongside trastuzumab and capecitabine, which act in different ways. Its tablet schedule continues through the capecitabine break.
agents.watch: Report diarrhoea early, especially with poor intake. Liver tests and a full medicines review are important.
risks: Liver test changes or liver injury

agents.name: Capecitabine
agents.explanation: The body converts capecitabine into fluorouracil, which disrupts DNA and RNA processes needed for cell growth. Tablets are active chemotherapy; taking them at home still requires a clear monitoring and interruption plan.
agents.watch: Stop tablets and contact the team for significant diarrhoea, painful mouth ulcers, hand-foot soreness affecting activities, fever or dehydration. Chest pain needs urgent assessment. Do not restart until instructed.
risks: Severe early toxicity including DPD-related toxicity

agents.name: Trastuzumab
agents.explanation: Trastuzumab binds to the HER2 protein on cells and helps reduce HER2-driven growth and recruit immune activity. HER2 testing identifies the cancers for which this approach is used.
agents.watch: Attend planned echoes. Report breathlessness, ankle swelling, rapid weight gain or infusion symptoms.

context_label: Advanced / metastatic · previously treated HER2-positive breast cancer
purpose: The three medicines work together to control previously treated HER2-positive advanced breast cancer. Treatment is reviewed regularly for benefit, symptoms and side effects.
schedule_summary: Tucatinib twice daily every day; capecitabine twice daily on Days 1–14 then off on Days 15–21; trastuzumab every 21 days by IV infusion or a locally approved under-the-skin injection. Continue while beneficial and tolerated, with clinician-approved changes.

phases_title: Each phase in your treatment plan
phases_note: The order depends on the indication and your recovery. The whole-treatment map shows how local treatment and ongoing medicines relate to each other.
medicines_title: Your medicines and their different roles
timeline_note: Planned treatment days are distinct from broad possible symptom patterns. Symptoms can occur outside these bands.
safety_note: There are no guaranteed safe days. Fever, shivers, sudden illness, new breathing problems or severe symptoms need prompt advice on any day, including a treatment break.
teachback: Which medicines are you taking now? What changes in the next phase? Which checks are due and who reviews them before treatment?
consent_support: Discuss the active phase, supportive medicines, fertility / menopause, treatment alternatives, monitoring, urgent contacts and when the plan will be reviewed.
urgent_extra: Report new breathlessness, jaundice, marked bleeding, severe diarrhoea, inability to drink, chest symptoms or a severe rash promptly.

support.title: Support for this phase
support.text: Obtain a clear diarrhoea action plan and separate instructions for each tablet. Anti-sickness medicines and interactions require individual review.

support.title: Bloods and cardiac checks
support.text: FBC, renal, liver; DPD testing before capecitabine → Extra tests if symptoms / toxicity → Pre-cycle bloods and symptom review. Symptoms need assessment between visits.

support.title: Visits and practical support
support.text: Ask about travel, work, fertility, menopause, exercise and help at home. The team arranges and reviews clinical checks; the patient should not have to calculate the monitoring timetable.

support.title: Follow-up and bone health
support.text: If an aromatase inhibitor or ovarian suppression is prescribed, assess fracture risk and baseline DEXA as indicated. Repeat timing depends on the result, risk and bone treatment; it is not an automatic scan for everyone.

questions.q: What changes in the next phase?
questions.a: Tucatinib twice daily every day; capecitabine twice daily on Days 1–14 then off on Days 15–21; trastuzumab every 21 days by the agreed IV or locally approved SC route. Continue while beneficial and tolerated, with clinician-approved changes.
Your team should confirm the next test, who books it, and who reviews the result before treatment. The map shows expected intervals; it does not track completed tests.

questions.q: Does every scan follow a fixed schedule?
questions.a: Use consistent modalities; earlier imaging if concern. New symptoms can require earlier assessment.

Assess need for symptom or brain-directed treatment → Any concurrent RT needs an explicit plan → Do not assume capecitabine can continue with RT → Coordinate holds / restart with radiation team → Imaging and local treatment depend on disease site

evidence.title: HER2CLIMB · longer follow-up
evidence.intro: This explains the study setting and its meaning. Ask the team how the evidence applies to you.
evidence.population: HER2CLIMB studied previously treated HER2-positive advanced breast cancer and included people with brain metastases.
evidence.interpretation: Adding tucatinib helped delay cancer growth and improved survival compared with the other study group. The study does not predict an individual outcome or compare this combination with every newer treatment.

phases.label: Three-medicine treatment
phases.detail: The capecitabine break does not mean a tucatinib break. Your team may hold or adjust one medicine without applying the same change to all three. Trastuzumab route is agreed separately; the fixed SC dose must not be treated as an IV loading or maintenance dose.

day_groups.title: Your reference cycle
day_groups.body: Tucatinib twice daily every day; capecitabine twice daily on Days 1–14 then off on Days 15–21; trastuzumab every 21 days by IV infusion or a locally approved under-the-skin injection. Continue while beneficial and tolerated, with clinician-approved changes.
day_groups.action: Check the agreed prescription and contact the team for new symptoms. Restart only after the team confirms the plan.

chronology_notes.title: Checks and restart
chronology_notes.text: Keep the arranged blood / heart appointments. A calendar day alone does not authorise the next dose.

steps.title: Before dispensing
steps.text: Confirm blood tests, interactions, the exact tablet strengths and the plan for missed doses.

steps.title: Taking tablets
steps.text: Tucatinib twice daily every day; capecitabine twice daily on Days 1–14 then off on Days 15–21; trastuzumab every 21 days by the agreed IV or locally approved SC route. Continue while beneficial and tolerated, with clinician-approved changes.

steps.title: Review before restarting
steps.text: The team confirms blood results, side effects and the next prescription. Never double a missed dose or restart held treatment without advice.

steps.title: Trastuzumab visit
steps.text: Trastuzumab every three weeks with staff observation. IV treatment may use a cannula, PICC or port; the locally approved SC alternative uses an injection under the skin; no routine take-home infusion pump.

steps.title: Confirm the trastuzumab route
steps.text: Your team confirms IV infusion or the locally approved under-the-skin injection. The visit length, observation and missed-dose instructions differ; ask before switching. The injection has no loading dose.

details.title: Missed or vomited dose
details.text: Do not take an extra dose. Follow the medicine-specific instructions and ask the team if uncertain.

details.title: Safe handling
details.text: Swallow tablets whole, keep them in their original packaging away from children, and return unused tablets to pharmacy.

details.title: Practical arrangements
details.text: Confirm who supplies the tablets, who arranges tests, who reviews results and your urgent contact route.

details.title: Port insertion and removal
details.text: The line team explains placement, dressing care and when normal activities can resume. A port is accessed with a special needle during treatment. Removal of the implanted device is a separate planned procedure when no longer needed; do not remove or adjust it yourself.

details.title: PICC care and urgent line symptoms
details.text: A PICC usually needs regular dressing and flushing appointments even between treatments. Fever, redness, swelling, pain, leakage or damage requires prompt advice. Your hospital supplies the exact care instructions.

anatomy: Report diarrhoea early. Follow the separate tablet-hold instructions; reduced urine or dizziness needs prompt advice.
Painful redness or peeling affecting activity: stop capecitabine and contact oncology.
Keep three-weekly liver blood tests. Report yellow skin / eyes or dark urine.
Keep echoes. New chest pain: stop capecitabine and seek urgent assessment.
Fever, shivers or sudden illness: call promptly. Blood tests guide the next cycle.

monitoring_schedule.title: When checks happen
monitoring_schedule.note: Elapsed-time tests remain due if a cycle is delayed. The treatment team books, reviews and acts on results. Calendar timing alone does not authorise a dose.
